findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, disk full)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, e)) or propagate with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input (e.g. a name with commas causing column shift, or a non-numeric value) aborts the process instead of yielding a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and use parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ...) or use try_fold with typed error

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside a data-loading function that should be a pure or shell-boundary operation
findings.failure_mode: core logic leaks side effects, making the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and producing unexpected console output when called by consumers who do not want logging
findings.fix: remove println! from the data-loading path; if logging is needed, pass a callback or use the imperative shell layer above this function

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values outside u16 range (0..=65535) after the unwrap already succeeds on parse
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 parses successfully, then as u16 wraps to 4464, producing silently corrupt data with no error
findings.fix: parse directly to u16 via parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>() and return Result, or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err() for a checked narrowing

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses index 0 on a Vec built from split of a line that may be empty or whitespace-only
findings.failure_mode: empty line or single-field line causes panic via IndexOutOfBounds instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: use if let [first, ..] = parts.as_slice() or check parts.len() >= 1 before access, returning a typed error for malformed lines

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index 1 without checking that split produced at least 2 fields
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one comma-separated field causes panic via IndexOutOfBounds instead of returning a typed parse/shape error
findings.fix: check parts.len() >= 2 before accessing parts[1], or use split_once(',') and handle the two-field case explicitly

findings.problem: load_metrics performs file I/O (fs::read_to_string) and is marked pub, but has no Result type to signal failure — it is a shell-level function masquerading without proper error surface
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish I/O failure from data shape failure; the function mixes shell concerns with core data construction and has no ergonomic error handling path
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError> where MetricError is an enum distinguishing IoError and ParseError/ShapeError; move parsing logic into a pure core function load_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and keep load_metrics as the thin shell that reads then delegates

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every single line, even when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations per line degrade throughput and increase memory pressure, especially for large files
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get two &str references directly, then trim only those two parts — zero intermediate Vec allocation

findings.problem: Record has pub fields with no validation at construction — name can be empty, value can be any u16
findings.failure_mode: invalid records (empty name, out-of-range value before fix) can be constructed freely, pushing validation to call sites
findings.fix: make fields private with a newtype constructor fn new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Self { ... } that rejects empty names and enforces invariants

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data for allocation hotspots in the CSV parsing path
no allocation tracking (e.g. alloc_counter, jemalloc stats) for this workload
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
no second-ring evidence (Miri, Kani, proptest) for panic-freedom on malformed input
residual_risk: This crate has 6 BLOCKER findings: unwrap on I/O and parse, silent truncation cast, two unchecked index accesses, and hidden I/O in a core-adjacent function. All blockers are fixable by returning Result types, using split_once, removing println, and parsing directly to u16. Without those fixes, any malformed CSV line or missing file will panic the calling process. No benchmarks or formal execution evidence exists.
